solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lace clothing of empress in photo call

indicators.note: the letters from empress go inside the word for a photo

parts.note: a shot is a photograph

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of empress are E and S
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A fashion shoot calls for a lace garment to be worn by an empress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing of empress' gives ES, which goes 'in' SHOT to make SHOEST; RING follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoestring is a shoelace, the cord used to tie a shoe.

clue.text: Cast piece of armour abandoned by lake

indicators.note: the lake letter is left behind, so it drops out

parts.note: a shield is a piece of armour
L = lake, removed

explanation.surface: A knight's bit of armour, cast aside and left by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as thrown off, which it is: to shy something is to throw it, so SHIED is the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy, so shied means cast.

clue.text: Some journalists in a group sent up key workers

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the run of letters inside journaliSTS IN A GROup

explanation.surface: A pack of reporters mocking the essential staff of a pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key workers' suggests essential staff; organists work keys on an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Organists play keyboards, so they are workers at keys.

clue.text: Ostracised soldier burying explosive around old bay

indicators.note: a word burying something holds it inside, so the soldier's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier standing guard

indicators.note: the explosive goes around the old bay, enclosing it

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, the explosive
a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A soldier buries a bomb near an old bay and is shunned by his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: TNT around O + COVE gives TOCOVENT, which goes inside SENTRY after SENT. Sent to Coventry is a British idiom for being ignored by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deliberately ignored and shut out by a group, which is what being ostracised is.

clue.text: Lots of ferries originally circled by shoal quickly list

indicators.note: take the original, first letter of each word

parts.note: a shoal is a sandbank or reef

indicators.note: the reef goes around those letters

parts.note: first letters of Lots Of Ferries

explanation.surface: A fleet of ferries trapped behind a sandbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' applies to all three words before it, not just 'ferries'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from fishing: line spinning off a reel, so a speaker rattling items off without pause.

clue.text: Males recalled wings of enormous island deity

indicators.note: called back, so the word for males is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: men are males

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: the end letters of enormous are E and S

explanation.surface: Men remember the giant flanks of a god worshipped on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN 'recalled' is NEM; the 'wings of' enormous are ES; IS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so she is a deity.

clue.text: Drop beer on the counter

indicators.note: running counter to the normal direction, so backwards

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: Spilling a pint on the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a bar top; it means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to drop, as prices slip or a standard drops.

clue.text: Master essentially coerces spare guards

indicators.note: the outer word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: lean and spare both mean thin

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle

parts.note: the middle letter of coeRces

explanation.surface: A slave-owner forcing a thin servant to stand guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a noun at the start; it is the verb, to get the hang of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: getting the hang of a subject, not the noun for a boss.

clue.text: Picked up harmony note inside of hall gradually

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, heard, so a sound-alike

parts.note: peace is harmony, and sounds like piece
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: take the letters from the inside of the word

parts.note: the inner letters of hALl

explanation.surface: Hearing a harmonious note slowly fill a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical words (harmony, note, hall) all point to a concert; only 'harmony' is heard, the rest are read.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means bit by bit, gradually.

clue.text: Snag small navel decoration perhaps on black hair

parts.note: S = small
bling (flashy jewellery) on a tum (tummy) is a navel decoration, like a belly-button ring
B = black, as on pencils
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Catching a tiny belly-button piercing in someone's dark hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags TUM BLING as one invented example of navel decoration rather than a dictionary phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a hidden difficulty that trips a plan up, which is the unexpected-problem sense of snag.

clue.text: Green female wearing uniform pressed by Vincent?

parts.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'

indicators.note: the uniform letter is squeezed inside Vincent's first name

parts.note: Gene Vincent was an American rock and roll singer
U = uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman whose uniform has been ironed by someone called Vincent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vincent?' wants Van Gogh; the question mark says Vincent is a surname here, so GENE. Green means naive.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, inexperienced young woman, a green female.

clue.text: Setter and former land owner lower emission

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a thane held land from a king in Anglo-Saxon and Scottish times

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter and an old laird cutting their carbon output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as a verb, to reduce emissions; it is an adjective, emission from the lower body, a wind joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is released when a person or a cow breaks wind, an emission from the lower end.

clue.text: Fellow American is not moving drawings from vessels?

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American academic's drawings stay put when taken from ships.
explanation.walkthrough: IS NOT 'moving' gives TIONS. The definition plays on blood being drawn from blood vessels, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood donations are drawn from donors' veins, which are blood vessels, so the phrase cryptically describes gifts of blood.

clue.text: Vicar's digs maybe woman senses to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used

parts.note: inside woMAN SEnses

explanation.surface: A woman partly picking up on something odd at the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' because a manse is strictly a Scottish or Nonconformist minister's house, not a vicar's; digs are lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a clergyman's house, so a vicar's lodgings, broadly.

clue.text: Radical writer introducing case for aesthetics

indicators.note: the writer has the letters put into its middle, as if introduced inside

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

indicators.note: the case for a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of aesthetics are A and S

explanation.surface: An extremist author puts forward an argument in favour of aesthetics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case for' aesthetics, AS, goes inside BIC, the writer 'introducing' it. 'Radical' here means fundamental, not extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical in the sense of root or fundamental is a synonym of basic, as in a basic change.

clue.text: Ceramic hob in Caen needing repair

indicators.note: the letters are broken and must be put back together differently

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A cooker hob in a French kitchen that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: Caen is a city in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: porcelain made with bone ash belongs to the wider class of fired pottery.

clue.text: Bond catches one youth crossing large barrage

indicators.note: the bond word catches the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: to fuse is to bond things together, so FUSE

indicators.note: the pair one and youth stretch across the large letter, sitting either side of it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a lad is a youth
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: James Bond grabs a young man crossing a large barrier, or similar spy action.
explanation.walkthrough: I and LAD sit either side of L to give ILLAD, which goes inside FUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a burst of many shots fired at once, the same thing as a barrage of fire.

clue.text: Artist is overwhelmed by shock valuation

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something puts these pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: to appal is to shock
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is stunned by a shocking assessment of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and IS go inside APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment of something's worth, which is a valuation.

clue.text: New tree beginning to leaf inside of foul city

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

indicators.note: inside of means the letter goes within the word for foul

parts.note: vile means foul, disgusting

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gardening note: a young tree's first leaf comes out inside something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tree' and 'leaf' make a botanical picture, but only ASH is a synonym; 'beginning to' leaf supplies just its first letter, set 'inside of' the word for foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee, famous as the home of country music.

clue.text: Throw back mostly what may have been in pot

definitions.text: what may have been in pot

parts.note: to lob is to throw
STERN, the back of a boat, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Tossing back most of a catch from a fisherman's pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw back' reads as one phrase about returning a fish; split it, and 'back' is the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint by example: lobster pots are the traps crustaceans are caught in, and 'may have been' allows for a cooking pot too.

clue.text: Wandering about over grass covering centre of domicile

indicators.note: in a down answer this piece sits on top of the following one, covering it
over here means turned over, so the letters for about are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to rat is to grass, to inform on someone

indicators.note: the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of domicile are I and C

explanation.surface: Someone roams about over the lawn that covers the middle of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: RE turned 'over' is ER; RAT sits on the 'centre of' domicile, IC, 'covering' it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means moving irregularly without a fixed course, like something straying or roaming.

clue.text: Pole joining another cycling in country

indicators.note: joining says the second piece is attached straight after the first

parts.note: N is the north pole

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter round to the front of the word

parts.note: a pale is a stake, so another kind of pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man rides a bike with a companion across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another pole, a pale or stake; 'cycling' its last letter to the front gives EPAL, 'joining' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan nation between India and China.

clue.text: Inexperienced person covering for archdeacon from island

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: the outside letters of ArchdeacoN

explanation.surface: A novice cleric standing in for the archdeacon on an island parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering for' reads as deputising; it means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective of origin: the definition is vague on purpose, and any Caribbean island native would fit until the wordplay narrows it.

clue.text: Temperature lowered in public pool for Thai rhino

indicators.note: in says the letter goes back inside the remaining word
lowered says the temperature letter is taken from its place so it can drop further down

parts.note: public baths are a municipal swimming pool

explanation.surface: The water temperature is reduced at the municipal swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: T is 'lowered' from BATHS, leaving BAHS, and goes back 'in' one place later. 'Rhino' is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the currency of Thailand, and rhino is slang for money, so bahts are Thai cash.

clue.text: Twisted bone by sewer blocked by British fool

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters run backwards
the sewer has the British letter stuck inside it

parts.note: a rib is a bone
a drain is a sewer
B = British

explanation.surface: A crooked bone found in a drain that a British idiot has clogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' here reverses rather than rearranges; with three letters the difference barely shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: someone supposedly with a brain as small as a bird's.

clue.text: Tense in verse one periodically raised by Yankee

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last letter is put beside the rest
in a down answer, raising letters means reading them upwards
taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter

parts.note: every other letter of VERSE ONE, starting with the first, gives V, R, E, N
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tense moment in a poem raised by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking verse one 'periodically' gives VREN, which 'raised' reads NERV; Y goes 'by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy means anxious and on edge, which is what tense describes.

clue.text: Take over in the air when flying without introduction of adult

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a fresh order
without means the letter is left out
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of adult is A

explanation.surface: An airborne craft takes control without an adult to introduce it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without introduction of adult' removes A from IN THE AIR, leaving INTHEIR, and 'when flying' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit something is to take it over from a predecessor, as an heir succeeds.

clue.text: Nick emptied tanker by one river after another

indicators.note: the second river follows the first
the insides are removed, leaving the ends

parts.note: TankeR with its middle removed
the Ouse is one of several English rivers
R = river

explanation.surface: An empty oil tanker stolen as it moved from one river to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for steal, and so is trouser, to pocket money.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser is to pocket money, often dishonestly, so to nick it.

clue.text: Primate keeping close to bars vaulted enclosure

indicators.note: the primate holds the letter inside

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of barS

explanation.surface: A zoo ape right up against the bars of its cage.
explanation.walkthrough: The zoo scene makes 'enclosure' a cage; it is the curved end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted, semicircular recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Good lines within contest important for future princess

indicators.note: the lines go inside the word for important

parts.note: G = good
a race is a contest
key means important
L = line, doubled for lines

explanation.surface: A royal-to-be learning her lines for an important part.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Kelly was a Hollywood actress who married Prince Rainier of Monaco in 1956, hence future princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace Kelly became Princess Grace of Monaco, so as an actress she was a future princess.
